Challenge yourself with today's puzzles.

There is nothing more quietly satisfying than being tanned. In the Eighties we did this the hard (and dangerous) way, a lick of SPF 2 tanning oil and full exposure until our skin was blistered. In the Nineties we were introduced to fake tan, as were our sheets and the palms of our hands. There was a brief hiatus in the Noughties, when tans became unfashionable and Gwyneth Paltrow went to the beach in a full cover-up. Thankfully that nonsense is behind us and a bronzed bod is once again encouraged. The difference is that these days there are skilled professionals who have taken up the task of making us look tanned. Here are some of the best….

Zip up to the sixth floor of the W Hotel in Leicester Square and you will find the Away Spa and a kind soul who also happens to be one of the worlds best tan artists. Known as the “Tom Ford of tanning”, James Harknett is responsible for the glowing skin of celebrities such as David Gandy and Emma Willis. Harknett is famed for his flawless tanning techniques that includes bespoke colour matching to client’s skin tone and even contouring (so you will walk away not only bronzed but with pronounced cheekbones and a six pack you didn’t know you had).

Harknett has worked as a tan artist for more than two decades. He does 50 spray tans a week and over 500 brides a year. He also works on film sets creating the optimum movie-star glow. His career started with the St Tropez brand — helping to develop the product into the success it is today. And though he still vouches for St Tropez, his current favourite is Three Warriors. If you want your summer skin to be perfect, Harknett is your artist.30 minute spray tan is £85, jamesharknett.co.uk

Jimmy Coco is fearless. Imagine applying a spray tan in a Mayfair hotel suite so pristine and expensive they usually ban red wine — all while wearing crisp white jeans and an LA-style, half-buttoned white shirt. That takes real nerve. But then, so does dealing with his roster of mega A-list clients daily. Known as the man behind the Kardashians’ signature year-round Hollywood glow, Coco also recently transformed Daisy Edgar-Jones’ English rose complexion into a sun-kissed shimmer for this year’s Met Gala.

Coco, whose real name is Jimmy Snyder, is usually found working from his LA Studio, where slots at his Beverly Hills site start from £260 ($350). But he offers home visits where he will bring all his tanning kit, from the tent to the tiny tanning pants, to you. His business also still operates out of London and he is often in town, whether that’s for his recent residency at 1 Hotel Mayfair or when he’s busy tanning celebrities for the Baftas or working with models for London Fashion Week. His tans are a world away from my previous spray-tan horror stories: no biscuit smell, no mahogany guide shade, no stickiness, and definitely no “tiger bread” patchiness before the necessary exfoliation to remove it a few days later. Coco treats spray tanning as an art form, even using darker shades to expertly sculpt jawlines and create the illusion of perfect abs. His own product line, Sunless, has an appealing scent with notes of cedarwood and apple. Best of all, the dreaded post-event phase is gone; about a week after the initial spray, the bronze has simply diffused into a subtle, honeyed shade, free of streaks or dry patches. Plus, I can even easily maintain the look using Jimmy Coco’s at-home products — ideal for those who aren’t rich and famous and don’t have him on speed dial.jimmycoco.co.uk

“We can’t wait to paint you” is written on the glass window of Iris Avenue. This is not a portrait studio but a beauty salon full of different kinds of artists. Nail artists. Brow and lash artists. And tan artists. On entering the salon (or what the company refers to as the “beauty bar”) you will find a chic waiting area and a gold-tiled bar serving lattes, smoothies and cocktails. As you proceed — negroni in hand — you will pass the nail studio area with its individual marble-effect tables and plush navy banquette benches. Downstairs are peach-coloured armchairs where customers can relax while having a pedicure.

It is this floor that houses the treatment rooms for massages, lashes, microblading and, of course, tanning. After undressing you step into the classy tiled shower cubicle ready to be sprayed with the utmost care. The tan artists (using Sienna X tan) only need 20 minutes of your time to ensure they get every nook and cranny — no knuckle wrinkle left pale. You will walk out darker in colour but lighter in feeling. £55 for full-body spray tan, irisavenue.com

There is surely nothing more fabulous than getting a beauty treatment without even having to leave the house? From the time the doorbell rings, it’s less than five minutes till the tanning tent is up and the tan artist is ready with the spray gun. You can expect to be choreographed into various shapes enabling the artist to reach every spot of skin. Unlike most tans, however, you can opt for the express tan that bronzes your skin in half the time meaning no overnight sheet (and relationship) ruining. The specific products vary from artist to artist but often they will use Sienna X too.

This beauty concierge service offers everything from tans to nails to massages all in the comfort of your home. And bookings are made through the Ruuby app. The luxury is in the ease of it all.From £45 or £50 for express tan, ruuby.com

The spa at Brown’s Hotel (which claims to be one of the oldest hotels in London) offers a two-step spray tan — an exfoliation followed by the application of the colour. Enter the grand Georgian building, catch a ride in the lift down to the basement level and when the elevator dings open you have arrived at the tranquil space of the spa. Using BeauBronz products, the first step is an exfoliation — a gentle spray to prime the skin, allowing the colour to go on evenly. The colour, expertly applied by the spa manager Olga, is warm but not orange, looks perfectly natural and is completely scent-free. Within 30 minutes you’ll step out into Mayfair with a luminous glow that lasts well over a week.£80 for 30 minutes, roccofortehotels.com
